Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Business and general-news outlets are overwhelmingly focused on the deepening AI-stock rout — with the Nasdaq 100 sliding into bear-market territory even after Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia failed to restore confidence — alongside the Trump administration's surprise new round of Section 301 tariffs on China, the EU, Japan and more than a dozen other economies. Secondary threads include hot inflation data keeping the Fed on a rate-hike path, Jamie Dimon's clash with the UK over bank taxes, and fallout from China's purge of Shanghai's party chief.

stories.headline: Nasdaq 100 Enters Bear Market as AI Trade Unravels
stories.summary: The Nasdaq 100 plunged for a second straight day into bear-market territory as traders dumped tech shares amid intensifying doubts about the sustainability of AI spending.

stories.headline: Anthropic's Record IPO Trade Is Already Unraveling
stories.summary: Anthropic, which staged the biggest IPO ever, fell below its offering price for a third straight session as the broader AI trade continued to crack.

stories.headline: Trump Unveils New Tariffs on China, EU and More Than a Dozen Other Economies
stories.summary: The administration proposed fresh Section 301 tariffs — including a 20% rate on China that could rise to 40% — targeting alleged industrial overcapacity, escalating trade tensions just as a Democratic-controlled Congress prepares to scrutinize presidential trade authority.

stories.headline: Hot Inflation Reading Keeps Fed on Track to Raise Rates
stories.summary: A fresh inflation report reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates again next month, adding another headwind for markets already rattled by the AI selloff.

stories.headline: Jamie Dimon Turns on Britain Over Bank Tax Hike
stories.summary: JPMorgan's chief executive is pushing back against the UK's cash-strapped government after it targeted banks for extra tax revenue, souring his once-warm relationship with Britain.

stories.headline: China Takes Down Shanghai Party Boss Once Seen as Potential Xi Successor
stories.summary: Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining, once viewed as a rising star, has been placed under investigation for suspected severe party-discipline violations, the latest in a string of high-profile purges.

stories.headline: College Graduates Increasingly Stuck in Jobs Below Their Degree Level
stories.summary: Underemployment among 22-to-27-year-olds has hit a six-year high, with graduates increasingly settling for low-paid retail or gig work rather than roles matching their degrees.

stories.headline: Retail Earnings Show Resilient Holiday Shopper, Led by Best Buy Beat
stories.summary: Best Buy posted its strongest comparable sales growth in five years and raised full-year guidance, part of a broader pattern of retail earnings beats pointing to resilient holiday consumer spending.

Business.gaps: No recent, on-topic items were found for The Information or Puck; Politico, Business Insider, BBC, The Economist, FT, WSJ and NYT coverage is limited to what appeared in the provided feed since direct search of those sites was not possible.

US politics.overview: Coverage across the group is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement and the national-security and corruption questions it raises for the Trump administration, alongside the rollout of sweeping new tariffs on China and the EU. Capitol Hill-focused outlets are also tracking a lame-duck permitting bill, the resignation of Rep. Jimmy Gomez after an ethics probe, and post-midterm turmoil inside the RNC, while immigration coverage centers on Kilmar Abrego García's departure for Spain.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's Nvidia reinstatement triggers bipartisan Capitol Hill backlash
stories.summary: Axios reports that Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO is drawing scrutiny from lawmakers in both parties, with Democrats vowing investigations into the Trump administration's role once they take power in January and Huang set to testify before House and Senate panels in early December.

stories.headline: Trump administration rolls out new tariffs on China, EU and other countries
stories.summary: The Hill reports the administration proposed fresh levies on more than a dozen countries, including a new 20 percent tariff on Chinese imports, in a move NYT frames as part of an ongoing trade escalation facing legal challenges and incoming Democratic scrutiny.

stories.headline: Kilmar Ábrego García leaves the U.S. for Spain, ending deportation fight
stories.summary: The Hill reports the Salvadoran migrant at the center of a long legal and political battle with the Trump administration arrived in Spain after opting to leave voluntarily rather than continue fighting deportation.

stories.headline: Rep. Jimmy Gomez to resign after sexual misconduct ethics probe
stories.summary: Roll Call reports the House Ethics Committee found substantial evidence against the California Democrat, prompting his resignation effective Dec. 1, a story also detailed by NPR.

stories.headline: RNC chair fights off midterm-loss challenge from within the party
stories.summary: Politico reports that Trump's handpicked RNC chair is fending off a challenge from a party colleague as Republicans look for someone to blame for their midterm losses.

stories.headline: Speaker Johnson eyes GOP unity as permitting bill vote nears in lame duck
stories.summary: Roll Call reports the long-awaited bipartisan energy permitting measure appears close to clearing the House, though some uncertainty remains among Republicans in the lame-duck session.

stories.headline: Appeals court rules lack of quorum invalidated House proxy voting
stories.summary: Roll Call reports a federal appeals court ruled that the Constitution's quorum requirement means pandemic-era House proxy votes were unconstitutional, a case with potential implications for past legislation.

stories.headline: Army proceeds with Iowa detonation of degraded lead azide stockpile
stories.summary: The Hill and Washington Examiner both covered the Army's decision to proceed with a controlled explosion of a degraded lead-based munitions stockpile in Iowa despite public health concerns.

US politics.gaps: No stories from the last 24-48 hours could be found for NOTUS or Cook Political Report via search; results returned were weeks to months old. Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian block web search, so only the specific feed items provided for those outlets were used.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets is dominated by a deepening Wall Street rout in AI-linked stocks, with Nvidia and newly-public Anthropic both tumbling as the broader 'AI trade' unwinds, alongside continued fallout from Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO amid the Megaspeed chip-smuggling scandal. Secondary threads include a wave of cybersecurity incidents hitting US government agencies, Microsoft's post-outage 'Code Red,' and jockeying between Big Tech AI agents (Amazon/Meta's Muse) and frontier labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepMind) rolling out new capabilities.

stories.headline: Nasdaq 100 enters bear market as AI trade unravels
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports the Nasdaq 100 fell into its first bear market in over a year as investors dumped AI-exposed stocks, with Nvidia and Anthropic both sliding sharply and Broadcom and Micron also hit hard.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's Megaspeed scandal still trails Nvidia's newly reinstated CEO
stories.summary: TechCrunch reports Huang still faces unresolved questions from Congress and Nvidia's own board over his relationship with an alleged chip smuggler tied to the Megaspeed affair, even as Trump floated a pardon as 'an option.'

stories.headline: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to end Muse AI shopping blockade
stories.summary: TechCrunch reports Amazon and Meta are discussing a deal that would end a two-month-long blockade preventing Meta's AI shopping agent Muse from operating on Amazon's marketplace.

stories.headline: Microsoft declares internal 'Code Red' after historic Outlook/Exchange outage
stories.summary: The Verge reports Microsoft triggered an unusual internal 'Code Red' after a nearly 24-hour Exchange Online and Outlook outage knocked out email access for users.

stories.headline: US financial crimes bureau FinCEN discloses cybersecurity incident amid wave of federal breaches
stories.summary: The Verge reports FinCEN, part of the Treasury Department, disclosed it is investigating a cybersecurity incident, part of a string of recent federal hacks and outages that also reportedly touched the CIA, NGA, and ODNI.

stories.headline: OpenAI preprint claims proof of long-standing matrix multiplication math problem
stories.summary: Techmeme flags an OpenAI preprint claiming to prove the matrix multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4, addressing a major open problem in theoretical computer science and mathematics.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind uses AI agents to speed up quantum algorithm design
stories.summary: DeepMind announced that agent teams combined with formal verification cut computing costs for quantum algorithms used in fusion energy and drug-related molecular simulation, including an 11.8x cost reduction for a fusion-related calculation.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to let AI agents approve code changes
stories.summary: Anthropic, fresh off its IPO, rolled out Claude Ship, a set of AI agents that can review, fix and even approve routine code changes, deepening its push to automate software development workflows.

Tech & AI.gaps: VentureBeat and IEEE Spectrum (beyond one unrelated executive profile) had no distinct recent AI/tech news surfaced in search; The Guardian had no relevant feed items or accessible recent coverage found.

Energy.overview: Coverage is dominated by the collapse of the COP31 climate talks in Antalya over fossil-fuel language, alongside a wave of stories on how AI-driven data center demand is reshaping power markets, stock valuations and utility deals. Oil markets are also in focus amid OPEC+ supply surplus expectations and renewed Middle East shipping risks.

stories.headline: COP31 climate talks collapse over fossil fuel language
stories.summary: Carbon Brief reports the Antalya summit failed to reach a 'pact' acceptable to all sides after a dispute over references to transitioning away from fossil fuels, with Carbon Brief journalists also hosting a live Q&A on the outcomes for food, forests and oceans.

stories.headline: AI power boom hits a reality check for energy stocks
stories.summary: WSJ says a sharp correction in power stocks tied to the AI buildout is creating buying opportunities for investors, a theme Latitude Media echoed in reporting on how Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's hands-on role in energy partnerships has whipsawed energy companies following Nvidia's earnings call and Anthropic's debut as a public company.

stories.headline: Oil prices swing on Middle East tensions and supply surplus fears
stories.summary: WSJ reports oil prices fell sharply as traders weighed an expected global supply surplus ahead of this weekend's OPEC+ meeting against renewed Middle East tensions, before rebounding the next day as shipping-risk concerns persisted.

stories.headline: Dangote's Nigerian refinery set to list in Lagos on December 1
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports billionaire Aliko Dangote's oil refinery is expected to begin trading on the Lagos exchange as soon as next week, with the Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals debut targeted for December 1.

stories.headline: FirstEnergy wins approval for $2.5B West Virginia gas plant
stories.summary: Consumer advocates and environmental groups opposed the project, citing concerns over load growth projections and shifting of project risk to ratepayers, but regulators approved FirstEnergy's utilities to build the gas plant anyway.

stories.headline: TVA touts $1.7B data center deal under new large-load tariff
stories.summary: Utility Dive reports TVA separately received the first small modular reactor construction permit from the NRC for a BWRX-300 reactor at the Clinch River Site in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, as it struck a major new data-center power deal.

stories.headline: PJM proposes overhaul of large-load interconnection process
stories.summary: Heatmap reports PJM Interconnection has proposed a new 12-month annual process to replace the 18- to 24-month study previously used to connect new generation and large power users like data centers, with applications potentially starting by late 2027 if FERC approves.

stories.headline: DOJ closes NextEra-Dominion antitrust probe as state hearings continue
stories.summary: The decision followed a promise by the utilities to allow ISO-NE's internal market monitor to investigate proposed plant retirements, even as executives faced pointed questions during ongoing hearings in Virginia.

Energy.gaps: Argus Media could not be checked within the search budget; Canary Media's most recent available content was over a week old; E&E News's site has stopped publishing new content and only returned outdated archives; Reuters, FT, NYT and The Economist block web search and no relevant feed items were provided for them this period.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across Chinese, Hong Kong, Taiwanese and international outlets is dominated by a widening Communist Party anti-corruption purge after Shanghai's party chief was placed under investigation, Huawei's conviction in a major US criminal trial, and Beijing's furious response to reports of fresh US tariffs just a week after the Trump-Xi summit. Business and trade press is also tracking a wave of Chinese EV and AI announcements, including a major BYD acquisition in France and new EU safeguard measures on hybrids.

stories.headline: Shanghai party chief Chen Jining placed under investigation
stories.summary: State-run Xinhua confirmed that Chen Jining, a Politburo member and Shanghai's party secretary who was widely tipped for promotion, is under investigation by China's top discipline and supervision bodies for suspected serious violations; Caixin notes he is the fourth Politburo member elected in 2022 to be probed, part of a tally of 61 senior officials investigated this year.

stories.headline: Huawei found guilty on 10 of 12 counts in landmark US trial
stories.summary: A Brooklyn federal jury convicted Huawei on bank and wire fraud, trade-secret conspiracy and sanctions-evasion charges tied to its Iran business after a years-long case, while acquitting it of the more serious racketeering and obstruction charges; Beijing immediately denounced the verdict as 'suppressing' Chinese firms.

stories.headline: US readies new tariffs on China and other economies, Beijing pushes back
stories.summary: Washington has reportedly proposed fresh tariffs on 14-16 economies including China just a week after the Trump-Xi summit in Shenzhen, prompting China's foreign ministry to call the prospect 'political maneuvering' and urge both sides to uphold their trade truce.

stories.headline: BYD in exclusive talks to acquire Ineos's French plant
stories.summary: BYD has entered exclusive negotiations to acquire Ineos Automotive's vehicle manufacturing plant in Hambach, France, with French President Macron confirming further details are expected in January.

stories.headline: EU to impose hybrid-car import quotas from December
stories.summary: The European Commission will introduce provisional safeguard quotas on hybrid vehicle imports for up to 200 days, set at roughly 15% above 2025 levels, with China urging Brussels to stick to prior consensus.

stories.headline: Huawei links domestic chip-design tools in live project
stories.summary: Huawei demonstrated a working toolchain linking Chinese electronic design automation software on an actual chip project, a step toward reducing reliance on foreign EDA tools amid US export curbs.

stories.headline: Hong Kong ticketing system hack exposes 1.3 million users' data
stories.summary: Hong Kong's government-run online ticketing platform was hacked, exposing data of 1.3 million users amid a broader surge in cybersecurity breaches across the city.

stories.headline: HKU may reconsider suspension of China human rights course
stories.summary: The University of Hong Kong's law school dean signaled he might revisit the sudden cancellation of a human rights in China elective, after students enrolled in the course were told it had been scrapped.

China.gaps: Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Rest of World, Yicai Global and Focus Taiwan had no China-politics/economy-specific recent items found in search or feeds; Reuters, AP and WSJ (beyond the one feed item) could not be searched directly due to access restrictions.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Middle East outlets is dominated by escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's oil and financial infrastructure, a fresh wave of tanker mine incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, and intensifying political fallout in Israel over a new October 7 inquiry and a deadly Gaza strike. Trade and tariff stories, including a new US tariff push and continued Gulf economic data, round out business coverage, alongside a deadly UAE road crash.

stories.headline: Houthis strike Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and Riyadh's PIF Tower again
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed renewed strikes on Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery at Ras Tanura and on Riyadh's PIF Tower for the second time in under a week, with Saudi civil defence reporting 11 people wounded in the tower attack and fires at the refinery complex.

stories.headline: Multiple oil tankers hit naval mines in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy reported a fresh string of tanker mine strikes in the Strait of Hormuz, part of a pattern of incidents in the strategic waterway that has unsettled shipping and oil markets.

stories.headline: Israeli strike kills Hamas official and family as UN warns of 'real threat' to Palestinians
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed a senior Hamas security official along with his wife and children in Gaza, as UN human rights chief Volker Turk warned of a growing risk of further atrocity crimes against Palestinians.

stories.headline: Knesset advances October 7 inquiry despite Netanyahu's objections
stories.summary: Israel's opposition-run parliament gave initial approval to an independent investigation into the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, a probe Prime Minister Netanyahu opposes.

stories.headline: US proposes new tariffs targeting China, India, EU and other trading partners
stories.summary: The Trump administration is planning tariffs on 14 economies it accuses of using subsidies to help industries overproduce, a move with implications for global trade flows including Gulf trading partners.

stories.headline: Iraq's top court rules Baghdad can deploy troops to secure Kurdistan borders
stories.summary: Iraq's highest court ruled that the federal government in Baghdad can deploy troops along all international borders, including those in the Kurdistan region, a decision with major implications for federal-Kurdish relations.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia's merchandise trade surplus grows sharply
stories.summary: Asharq Al-Awsat reported that Saudi Arabia's merchandise trade surplus grew by 74.5%, underscoring continued strength in the kingdom's export performance despite regional tensions.

stories.headline: UAE fleet operators tighten safety rules after deadly Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah crashes
stories.summary: Following two fatal road accidents that killed 27 people in Fujairah and Ras Al Khaimah, UAE commercial fleet operators are reinforcing driver-fatigue monitoring and vehicle inspections ahead of new nine-hour daily driving limits.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not retrieve current material specific to Arab News, Khaleej Times (beyond UAE/crash coverage), AGBI, Zawya, Al Arabiya English, Haaretz, Ynetnews or Iran International within the last 48 hours; FT, NYT, BBC, AP and Reuters content was limited to what appeared via feed items or other outlets' citations since direct search is blocked for some of these.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage is dominated by renewed violence in eastern DRC colliding with the country's dire Ebola outbreak, alongside major African business news including Dangote Refinery's imminent Lagos listing, a cobalt export ban roiling global markets, and a possible MTN-Telkom telecoms merger in South Africa. Several outlets also flagged the fallout from COP31's collapse for African climate finance and a deadly communal attack in Nigeria.

stories.headline: DRC rebel group CRP halts advance on Bunia after Ugandan-mediated talks
stories.summary: A rebel group led by convicted war criminal Thomas Lubanga withdrew from territory it had seized near Bunia in Ituri province after days of fighting with Congolese government forces, citing commitments made during Uganda-mediated talks.

stories.headline: WHO chief pleads for peace as fighting disrupts DRC's Ebola response
stories.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said heavy fighting near a hospital in DRC's Ituri province forced health workers to shelter for over 24 hours, disrupting the response to an outbreak that has killed thousands.

stories.headline: Dangote Refinery set to list in Lagos on December 1
stories.summary: Aliko Dangote's oil refinery is expected to begin trading on the Nigerian stock exchange as soon as next week, with the debut for Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals being set for December 1.

stories.headline: Congo reimposes cobalt export ban as prices slide, jolting global markets
stories.summary: Top cobalt producer DRC will reintroduce an export ban on the battery metal from the end of the month to reverse slumping prices, a move that sent China's cobalt futures surging to a three-month high.

stories.headline: Nigeria's Borgu district reels from deadly weekend communal attacks
stories.summary: Residents of Borgu district in central Nigeria were left dealing with the aftermath of communal violence that killed several dozen people over the weekend.

stories.headline: MTN's renewed Telkom takeover bid raises competition concerns
stories.summary: MTN's revived acquisition talks with Telkom could reshape South Africa's telecoms market, promising greater network investment but raising worries about competition and wholesale access.

stories.headline: COP31's collapse in Antalya leaves Africa without climate finance breakthrough
stories.summary: The COP31 summit in Antalya ended without an overarching climate pact after the EU rejected a deal that omitted fossil fuels, and analysts said Africa was left again without a grant-based climate finance commitment.

stories.headline: Zimbabwean preacher Uebert Angel appears in court in handcuffs over assault charge
stories.summary: The once politically-connected televangelist, a former special envoy to President Mnangagwa, appeared in court as prosecutors opposed bail citing flight risk; The Africa Report separately profiled his political rise and fall.

Africa.gaps: Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block direct web search and had no relevant Africa items in the supplied feed, so their current Africa coverage could not be verified beyond what Mining Weekly attributed to Reuters and Bloomberg wire copy.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past 48 hours is dominated by the fallout from Skydance's buyouts at CBS News and CNN, alongside publisher responses to AI—from Dow Jones blocking bots to Disney's internal AI push and Press Gazette's human-made certification. Legal and governance fights in entertainment (CNN's courtroom battles, the BBC-Trump suit, and UK's CIISA bullying watchdog) also feature prominently.

stories.headline: CBS' Beltway Buyouts
stories.summary: Status reports that the fallout from Skydance's buyout offers at CBS News keeps widening, with senior figures in the network's Washington bureau now confirmed to have quietly accepted exit packages after more than two dozen staffers left the London bureau.

stories.headline: The Wall Street Journal joins a growing list of publishers disallowing bots by default
stories.summary: Nieman Lab notes that Dow Jones has overhauled its bot strategy so that all crawlers are now blocked by default, joining a wave of publishers shutting out unwelcome bots.

stories.headline: CNN's Courtroom Hangovers
stories.summary: Puck's Dylan Byers reports that AT&T and Warner Bros. Discovery are now fighting each other over who should pay for a CNN libel settlement, with AT&T filing a countersuit over an obscure insurance dispute, while a separate Azerbaijan lawsuit could test whether a foreign government can sue a US news outlet at all.

stories.headline: As Bob Iger Exits Disney for Good, an Unwelcome Biography Arrives
stories.summary: The New York Times reports that a new biography, 'The House of Mouse,' challenges the carefully cultivated image of outgoing Disney chief Bob Iger just as he prepares to attend his final board meeting.

stories.headline: BBC Asks Appeals Court to Toss Trump's Defamation Lawsuit
stories.summary: TheWrap reports the British broadcaster is arguing on appeal that the documentary at the center of Trump's defamation case never aired in the United States.

stories.headline: Netflix Only Big Player Not Funding UK's Independent Bullying & Harassment Complaints Body
stories.summary: Deadline reports Netflix is the sole major industry player yet to contribute funding to the UK's anonymous whistleblowing service for bullying and harassment complaints, the Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority (CIISA), even as Variety reports a spike in whistleblowing reports to the watchdog following Russell Brand's rape conviction.

stories.headline: Josh D'Amaro Is Dragging Disney Into the AI Era, Kicking and Screaming
stories.summary: TheWrap's exclusive describes internal tension at Disney as new CTO Karandeep Anand tries to push a unified AI vision across the company's disparate business units.

stories.headline: Press Gazette is 'world's first' verified human-made news outlet
stories.summary: Press Gazette announced it has been certified by Made By Humans, which scans its content for signs of AI manipulation, positioning the outlet as a test case for human-authenticated journalism.

Media.gaps: No recent coverage found from WSJ, FT, Columbia Journalism Review, Poynter, Variety, The Hollywood Reporter, Adweek, Digiday, Mediaite, or The Guardian specifically on the top media-industry stories beyond what's listed; their recent output skewed toward entertainment/lifestyle or unrelated news not matching this group's focus.
